title: The Crusades (1095-1291)
key_facts: Series of religious wars between Christians and Muslims over Holy Land
Multiple major crusades: First (1095-1099), Third (1189-1192), Fourth (1202-1204)
Established temporary Christian kingdoms in Jerusalem and surrounding areas
Led to increased East-West trade and cultural exchange despite religious conflict
causes: Papal calls to reclaim Jerusalem and holy sites from Muslim control
European knights seeking land, wealth, and religious salvation
Byzantine Empire's request for Western military aid against Seljuk Turks
Religious fervor and pilgrimage routes threatened by Muslim expansion
outcome: Ultimately failed to permanently secure Christian control of Holy Land
Established lasting religious tensions between Christianity and Islam
Increased European contact with Islamic science and culture
Weakened Byzantine Empire and contributed to its eventual fall

figures.name: Pope Urban II
figures.role: Launched First Crusade at Council of Clermont

impacts: Increased religious intolerance and persecution in Europe
Stimulated European trade and banking systems for crusade financing
Contributed to the Renaissance through rediscovery of classical knowledge
Created lasting legacy of Christian-Muslim conflict in Middle East
